_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); net revenue, credit cost, expense, nonperforming-asset and pre-tax margin signals with JPMorgan Chase's rule-T thresholds

pit_profile.why: 'JPMorgan Chase & Co. ... is a leading global financial services firm and one of the largest banking institutions in the United States' 'JPMorgan Chase’s businesses are materially affected by economic and market conditions' 'The financial services industry is highly competitive, and JPMorgan Chase’s results of operations will suffer if it is not a strong and effective competitor.' (FY2017 10-K); DURABLE, risk 2: the 10-K ties results to markets and the economy, a cycle and a competitive field, and does not call its own business cyclical (the word appears only in 'countercyclical capital buffer', a regulatory term: the LOW and SHW reading); among its competitors it lists 'e-commerce and other Internet-based companies, financial technology companies', and it says 'both financial institutions and their non-banking competitors face the risk that payment processing and other services could be disrupted by technologies, such as cryptocurrencies, that require no intermediation'; no disruption theme in taxonomy_eras.json is live for a bank holding company on this date, so the watch list is empty and these words stay here (the PEP obesity rule)

classification.quality_note: 'JPMorgan Chase & Co. ... is a leading global financial services firm and one of the largest banking institutions in the United States' 'JPMorgan Chase’s businesses are materially affected by economic and market conditions' 'The financial services industry is highly competitive, and JPMorgan Chase’s results of operations will suffer if it is not a strong and effective competitor.' (FY2017 10-K); DURABLE, risk 2: the 10-K ties results to markets and the economy, a cycle and a competitive field, and does not call its own business cyclical (the word appears only in 'countercyclical capital buffer', a regulatory term: the LOW and SHW reading); among its competitors it lists 'e-commerce and other Internet-based companies, financial technology companies', and it says 'both financial institutions and their non-banking competitors face the risk that payment processing and other services could be disrupted by technologies, such as cryptocurrencies, that require no intermediation'; no disruption theme in taxonomy_eras.json is live for a bank holding company on this date, so the watch list is empty and these words stay here (the PEP obesity rule). durable franchise (obsolescence risk 2/5); price cheap; Ratio B 0.72x; +28% to EPP floor; model-vs-market gap +0.22; conservative 2yr +12%.

BEAR.desc: EPS -16.4%/yr (worst year FY08-FY18, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +7.1%/yr (Q4 revenue YoY + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr median

BULL.desc: EPS +26.2%/yr (FY08-FY18 CAGR, at least BASE); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +112.1%/yr (best 2-yr run FY08-FY18, at least BULL); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: JPM (retrospective, 2019-02-01) ◉ BUY — Ratio B 0.72x (52.2% downside to Bear $49.69 / +72.4% upside to Bull $179.12) | Adj composite 2.32 vs market 2.10: gap +0.22 [MODESTLY UNDERVALUED] | +28% above the EPP floor $81.00 (9x FY19E $9.00) | Conservative 2-yr case: +11.6% total (+5.8%/yr) | At 11.5x FY19E the 15% hurdle price $137.38 sits between the BASE and BULL cases; revenue +6.8% YoY in Q4 2018, forward revenues +6.8% (Q4 2018 revenue growth (no Q1 2019 guide)); no disruption theme has dated evidence.
